0.2.0.lead: AI programs can now do everything you can do in nexlore, and you decide per tool what they may do on their own. Spaces can be renamed, people appear under a name of their own choosing, and nexlore tells you when a newer version is out.

sections.title: AI from outside can do everything, with rights per tool
sections.where: Account menu, My account, AI, a key, Rights per tool
sections.body: Over MCP an AI program now makes spaces, folders and notes, renames and moves them with their links, and works with versions, the trash, tags, comments and attachments. Under each key you set every tool to Allow, Ask or Deny. New keys read freely, ask before they make or change something, and do not even see the tools that delete, share or change members. The operator can block tools for everybody.

sections.title: Approvals
sections.where: Account menu, Approvals, and New since your last visit
sections.body: A tool set to Ask waits for you. The request shows with exactly what the program sent; Approve and run does exactly that, Decline does nothing, and after 24 hours it runs out. With a tick the tool runs without asking from then on.

sections.title: Connectors
sections.where: My account, AI, How to connect a program
sections.body: Programs that sign in themselves need only the address of nexlore with /api/mcp after it. You sign in, choose the level and the spaces, and agree; the program then stands in the list like a key. For AI apps that run in the cloud, nexlore must be reachable from the internet; a program on your own computer reaches it at home.

sections.title: Rename a space
sections.where: Sidebar, right click on a space, Rename
sections.body: For the managers of a space. Links that name the space in front, like [[Space/Note]], follow in every space, and so do favorites, public pages, drafts and the home space of every account. Links without the name stay as they are.

sections.title: A display name for every account
sections.where: Account menu, My account, Profile, Display name
sections.body: Each account chooses how others see it, for example with first and last name. In member lists and in the @ suggestions the sign-in name stays beside it, because that is what goes into the text after @.

sections.title: About nexlore, with an update check
sections.where: Account menu, About nexlore
sections.body: The version, the licence, the source code and the releases. Once a day nexlore asks GitHub whether a newer version is out; only that question goes out. The operator can switch it off there and check by hand.

small: The settings moved into the account menu, as in Nexview; the header keeps the places you work in.
This window comes once per version with news, for every account.

0.3.0.lead: nexlore now tells you when something needs you: by webhook, and by mail when the operator set up a mail server. You choose for each occasion whether you hear about it.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.where: Account menu, My account, Notifications
sections.body: Give a webhook address, a notification inbox for example, and switch mail on if your operator set up a mail server. Then choose what you hear about: somebody names you with @ or answers in your thread, an invitation or an approval for an AI program waits, and once a day at a time of your choosing, what is due today or overdue. Send a test shows at once whether it arrives. A notification names the note and who did something, never what a note or a comment says.

sections.title: Server troubles reach the operator
sections.where: Account menu, My account, Notifications, Server troubles
sections.body: Operators hear when a scheduled backup failed, when a newer version of nexlore is out and when the disk where nexlore keeps its data runs full. Each of these comes once, not every minute.

small: Moving a note to the trash right after opening the dialog takes the files only this note uses along again; before, they could stay behind.

0.4.0.lead: nexlore now works with programs such as n8n and nexdeck. An API token reads your notes, tasks and the numbers for a dashboard, and if you want it also writes: makes, changes, appends, ticks off. It can never delete, move or share.

sections.title: API tokens for programs
sections.where: Account menu, My account, Connections, API tokens
sections.body: Make a token of its own for each program: read or write, for all your spaces or only some, and if you like running out after 30 days, 90 days or a year. The token is shown once, with the header line for n8n and a command to try it. What a program writes becomes a version with the source “Program (API)”; when the note changed meanwhile or somebody is editing it, the text goes into a conflict copy.

sections.title: The operator holds the latch
sections.where: Settings, Server, AI, API and plugins, API tokens
sections.body: API tokens are off by default. The operator switches them on, sees every token with its account, level and last use, never the token itself, and can block one for good. Switched off, every token answers 401 until they are switched on again.

small: A week before one of your API tokens runs out, it stands out in yellow in the list, and nexlore tells you (My account, Notifications, can be switched off).
The part of the server settings is now called “AI, API and plugins”.

0.4.1.lead: A link to a heading now takes you right there, and a few things that did not work as they should are repaired.

sections.title: Links jump to the heading
sections.where: Any note with a link like [[Note#Heading]]
sections.body: A click on a link to a heading no longer opens the note at the very top but right at that heading, while reading as in the editor, and on the title of an embedded part too. Upper or lower case does not matter. If you leave out the note's name, as in [[#Heading]], you jump within the same note.

small: A link like [[#Heading]] no longer shows pale as a missing note, and cleaning up no longer lists it among the links to nothing.
The detail of the log can be turned up for an hour again; before, the choice quietly fell back.
Callouts of the kinds question, help and faq are yellow in the editor as when reading, no longer violet.
A few texts still named the old way “My account, AI”; they now lead through Connections.

1.0.0.lead: nexlore 1.0. Before this version it went through a large security review with one question: what happens when you open nexlore to the internet? What came out is in here: a fresh server nobody else can claim, a sign-in strangers cannot use to lock you out, and no way into your home network through nexlore.

sections.title: The first start asks for a code
sections.where: The setup page, the first time you open nexlore
sections.body: Whoever reached a fresh nexlore first used to become its operator. Now the setup page asks for a code that nexlore writes to its log when it starts (docker logs nexlore), or the one you set as NEXLORE_SETUP_TOKEN. Servers already set up notice nothing.

sections.title: Guessing passwords cannot keep you out
sections.where: Sign-in
sections.body: After ten wrong passwords an account still waits a quarter of an hour, but the browser you signed in with before gets in anyway: a stranger's guesses lock the account against the world, not against you. The brake now counts per sender and name, so one person guessing behind your proxy no longer slows everybody else.

sections.title: AI services in your own network, by name
sections.where: Settings, Server, AI, API and plugins, AI in notes
sections.body: Members may use any public AI service. A service in your own network (Ollama at home, for example) works once you list its host under Services in your own network; every other address there is refused, so nobody can reach your router or NAS through nexlore. If your members already use one at home, add it there.

sections.title: Backups ask for your password
sections.where: Settings, Server, Backups
sections.body: Deleting a backup and going back to one now ask for your password once more, as downloading did. Backups, the database and the log are readable only for nexlore's own user.

sections.title: Pictures and files in the sidebar
sections.where: Sidebar, inside a folder
sections.body: Pictures, PDFs and other attachments now stand in the tree beside the notes, and a folder counts them too. A click opens the file's page; the right click renames it (the ending stays), moves it, copies a link that embeds it or puts it in the trash.

small: A new password, or Sign out everywhere, also ends every program that signed in over OAuth; a refresh token used twice ends its program, and programs sign in again after 90 days.
An approval runs once, however often it is clicked, and a program never has the operator's powers.
Display names cannot pass for another account any more.
Notes written to slow nexlore down (thousands of open brackets, deep quotes, YAML aliases, endless headings) are read quickly now, on the server and in the browser; the reading view never goes blank.
At most 60 notifications an hour reach one account, and invitation mails need the public address.
The README has a checklist for running nexlore on the internet.
The language picked in the account menu holds the first time; on a slow server it used to switch back.

1.1.0.lead: nexlore 1.1 brings the canvas: a surface without edges for notes, thoughts, pictures and links, joined by arrows. It lies as a .canvas file beside your notes, in the open format JSON Canvas, and Obsidian opens it just the same.

sections.title: Making a canvas
sections.where: Sidebar, right-click a folder or a space, New canvas …
sections.body: A new canvas is empty and lies in the folder you make it in. The guide has chapter 14 on it and an example canvas to try things on.

sections.title: Notes as cards
sections.where: On the canvas, Note at the bottom, or drag a note in from the sidebar
sections.body: A note card shows the note, or only one of its sections. A double click opens it beside the canvas in the editor you know; what you write there shows on the card right after. Rename the note and the canvas follows.

sections.title: Writing right on the card
sections.where: On the canvas: double-click an empty spot or a text card
sections.body: Text cards are edited in place with the same editor as notes. The bar over chosen words and the slash menu keep their size, however far you zoom.

sections.title: Arranging with snapping
sections.where: On the canvas, drag cards; the magnet at the top right turns it off
sections.body: Edges and middles snap to other cards and guides show it; not with Alt held while dragging. Groups take along what lies in them, and arrows run from edge to edge with a label if you like.

sections.title: Arrows find their way
sections.where: On the canvas: drag from a point on the edge of one card to another
sections.body: Arrows run around the cards in their way at right angles and turn halfway between two cards. Their label stays readable however far you zoom out. The file keeps only the two sides; other programs draw the same arrow their own way.

sections.title: Cards from other spaces
sections.where: Drag a note from another space in from the sidebar, or Note at the bottom
sections.body: A card may come from any space you may read; its space stands in the head of the card, and Show in the sidebar takes you to it. Whoever may not read that space sees the card locked and nothing of what it holds.

small: Before deleting, the dialog names the canvases something lies on. The card stays there and shows it again as soon as you bring it back from the trash.

Drag the right edge of the sidebar to make it wider or narrower, and every row shows its whole name under the pointer. Canvases and views stand among the favourites with their name and their own symbol.
Take a space to another nexlore: right-click it in the sidebar, Download as ZIP, and there Import a ZIP as a space under Files. Every file comes along; versions, comments and members stay behind.
AI in notes said the service could not be reached although the key was valid. nexlore now also reads the packed answers some services send longer lists in.
A space at the start of a line showed as a tag “#x20” when reading.
A note names the canvases it lies on among its backlinks.
Canvases have versions like notes; bring an older one back from Versions at the top.
Far out, cards show only their title.
On a phone you read canvases, edit text cards and open notes.

1.2.0.lead: nexlore 1.2 is about the map. Choose which spaces it shows, and a space you fill one note at a time now grows on the map as it fills.

sections.title: Only the spaces you want on the map
sections.where: Map, the list of spaces at the top right (on a phone behind the button at the top right)
sections.body: Each space has a box: untick it and the map leaves the space out. Only this one, next to a name, shows that space alone; Show all brings every space back. The choice is kept with your account, so it is the same on every device, and each space keeps its colour. Pick a note of a space left out in the sidebar or a search, and its space comes back onto the map.

sections.title: A space filled bit by bit keeps its shape
sections.where: Map
sections.body: A space that was nearly empty when the map first laid it out, and then got its notes one at a time (by hand or by an AI helper through MCP), stayed a tiny bubble: its folders piled up at the edge and its notes lay in a spiral in the middle until the night put them in order. Now the map lays such a space out anew as soon as a new folder or note finds no room in it, and after many notes added one by one.

small: With many spaces, the sheet with clouds and spaces on a phone scrolls in itself; on a low screen its top used to lie out of reach.

A second nexlore set up with the authentik button on the same authentik takes names of its own (nexlore (address)) instead of taking over the first one's provider, which broke the first one's sign-in.
The preview of a comment no longer closes when the sidebar moves by itself, only when its words scroll away.

1.3.0.lead: nexlore 1.3 is about backups. A downloaded backup goes back in, so you move to a new server in the interface, and the backups card is tidied up.

sections.title: Upload a backup, move to a new server
sections.where: Settings, Server, Backups, "Upload a backup"
sections.body: Download a backup on the old server, set up nexlore on the new one and upload the ZIP there: it appears in the list as "uploaded", you check it and restore it. After the restart you sign in with your old account, and every space, note, attachment and account is there. Uploading asks for your password like downloading, and the automatic clean-up leaves uploaded backups alone.

sections.title: The backups card, tidied up
sections.where: Settings, Server, Backups
sections.body: The schedule, how many backups stay, uploading and "Back up now" share one row. Every backup has small buttons to check, download, restore and delete it; a window of its own asks for the password. Up to 365 backups can be kept now. A note for a new backup is gone; the notes of older backups still show in the list.

small: The guide's chapter on backups and moving in explains how to move a whole server.

1.4.0.lead: nexlore 1.4 brings Ask Lore: questions about your notes, answered from them with their sources. Writing in Markdown has a view of its own, and the map has a new look that moves.

sections.title: Ask Lore
sections.where: The spider at the bottom right of every page, or Ask Lore in the header
sections.body: Ask about your notes in a chat window, such as "When was the last restore test?". Lore looks in the spaces you may read, answers from them as she writes, and puts a small number after every statement: a click shows the source, another opens the note there. What your notes do not say, Lore says plainly. On a note the window talks about that note and can leave a change on it as a proposal, which you compare and take over or leave. An answer can become a note of its own. Your conversations are yours only.

sections.title: One AI service for everybody
sections.where: Settings, Server, AI, API and plugins, AI in notes
sections.body: The operator switches Ask Lore on and chooses whether every account brings its own AI service or one service serves all, such as Ollama at home. With one for all and a model for meaning, Lore also finds notes that say your question in other words, and the tab Links beside a note shows the notes most like it.

sections.title: The Markdown view
sections.where: While editing, the switch Visual | Markdown in the toolbar; Settings, General, Editor
sections.body: The Markdown view stands on the page like the visual editor and keeps the whole toolbar: bold, lists, headings and links put the signs into the text for you, and undo takes them back. One click on Visual and you are back. Under Settings, General you choose which view your notes open in.

sections.title: The map, new
sections.where: Graph
sections.body: Move over a note: it and its neighbours stay bright, the rest steps back, its links light up. The more links a note has, the bigger its dot. Linked notes draw together inside their folder, folders lie as a faint circle behind their notes, and the wheel glides. Drag a note with the mouse and its neighbours swim along; it stays where you let go until you reload the page.

small: Lines no longer disappear when you zoom into a space with many links.
The soft glow around the dots of the map can be switched off under Settings, Looks, for older computers.
The guide explains Ask Lore, the Markdown view and the new map.

1.5.0.lead: nexlore 1.5 reads PDFs itself and puts notes on paper: a PDF opens in nexlore instead of downloading, and any note, or a whole folder, becomes a neatly set PDF.

sections.title: Read PDFs in nexlore
sections.where: A click on a PDF in the sidebar, or on a link to a PDF
sections.body: The PDF opens with pictures of its pages and its own contents on the left; you turn pages, zoom and find text. The chain link copies a link to the page, such as [[Manual.pdf#page=3]], and a click on it opens the PDF right there. On the right you see which notes link the PDF, and to which pages, and Note on this PDF makes a note that opens beside it.

sections.title: PDFs in a note
sections.where: In a note ![[Manual.pdf#page=3]], when reading and when editing
sections.body: An embedded PDF shows as a small reader to page through, as tall as you like with #height=400. A PDF also opens beside a note: you read on the right and write on the left, and a page link in the note turns the PDF there.

sections.title: Print and save as PDF
sections.where: The ⋯ menu of a note, Print … or Save as PDF …; for a folder, its menu in the sidebar
sections.body: The window shows the pages as they come on paper, and every choice at once: paper, properties, embedded notes, web addresses as footnotes, header and footer, font. A folder becomes one PDF with a cover and contents, where links between its notes can be clicked. Paper is always light.

small: Programs fetch a note or a folder as PDF through the API (/api/v1/note/pdf, /api/v1/folder/pdf).
A PDF runs in a sandboxed frame without an origin of its own and without any network; the page hands it the file.
